digest.component_or_area: reconciliation engine - binding lifecycle and outbound mutation
propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer in production because differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes only fires when local_state entries carry a jira_key field, but run_differs passes a fetched Jira snapshot whose entries never carry jira_key, making all downstream consumers dead code.

Once a confirmed-404 retires a binding after 3 consecutive note_absent calls, _retire removes it from bindings and reverse, causing get_jira_key to return None and outbound_differ to emit a fresh CREATE for the unbound local ticket, resurrecting the deliberately-deleted issue.

The operator ruling forbids resurrection of deleted Jira issues; the guard must suppress outbound CREATE for local tickets whose binding was retired on a confirmed 404, while allowing never-bound tickets to create normally.

The dead legacy chain (probe producer, inbound_probe.py, route_inbound_probe, _apply_inbound_delete, create_after_hard_delete) must be removed, with BindingStore.unretire() and is_retired_local() added as reversible escape hatches and observability hooks.

The dormant absence-probe port capability (probe_remote, SupportsAbsenceProbe, inbound_probe.py) is retained with a follow-up because both Cloud and DC adapters implement it and epic e369 AC5 claims shared classify_probe_response usage.
